extra_checks.b_race_tests_deterministic: Deterministic. Both tests log with a custom CallbackState (IReadOnlyList<KeyValuePair>) whose indexer runs a one-shot callback on its first read, i.e. while LogBufferingFilterRuleSelector.Select is enumerating the candidate list and matching attributes. The callback runs synchronously on the same thread: config.Reload() in WhenConfigUpdatedWhileSelectingRule_DoesNotThrow, and otherRequest.Dispose() (a scope whose IncomingRequestLogBuffer.Dispose used to call the shared InvalidateCache) in WhenOtherRequestEndsWhileSelectingRule_DoesNotThrow. No threads or timing are involved. At BASE this clears the pooled List being enumerated, so they fail every time; with the fix they passed 20/20 each on net9.0 and net10.0.
extra_checks.c_remaining_uses: grep over src, test and bench (there is no samples folder): LogBufferingFilterRuleSelector appears only in GlobalBuffer.cs, PerRequestLogBufferManager.cs, IncomingRequestLogBuffer.cs, its own file, and LogBufferingFilterRuleTests.cs, all with the new shape (ctor(rules), Select(level, eventId, attrs)). No DI registration of LogBufferingFilterRuleSelector remains. The remaining InvalidateCache hits are LogSamplingRuleSelector/RandomProbabilisticSampler, a different class that this change does not touch. Constructor call sites: new GlobalBuffer only in GlobalLogBufferManager (both #if branches updated); GlobalLogBufferManager and PerRequestLogBufferManager are created only by DI (TryAddSingleton / ActivatorUtilities.CreateInstance(sp, globalBufferManager)); new IncomingRequestLogBuffer only in PerRequestLogBufferManager. No test or bench constructs them directly. All of these projects, including bench/Libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Telemetry.PerformanceTests and Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics.Middleware.PerformanceTests, are built by ./build.sh (0 Error(s)), and Telemetry built for net462/netstandard2.0/net8.0/net9.0/net10.0.
extra_checks.d_perrequest_manager_dispose: Registration: TryAddSingleton(sp => ActivatorUtilities.CreateInstance<PerRequestLogBufferManager>(sp, globalBufferManager)) plus TryAddSingleton<LogBuffer>(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<PerRequestLogBufferManager>()) and TryAddSingleton<PerRequestLogBuffer>(same). Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection captures a factory result for disposal once per registration that resolves it. A console probe against the built assemblies (net10.0) resolved ILoggerFactory, PerRequestLogBuffer, LogBuffer and the manager, then counted the manager in the root scope's _disposables list: it is captured 3 times. So the container disposes it up to 3 times (once per forwarding registration that was resolved), not exactly once. This is harmless: Dispose only calls OptionsMonitor<T>.ChangeTrackerDisposable.Dispose, which removes the listener and is idempotent. provider.Dispose() plus an extra manual Dispose() threw nothing. GlobalLogBufferManager is registered with the same forwarding pattern at BASE. The with-fix test outputs (6 full runs) contain no ObjectDisposedException apart from the existing test name RequestHeadersEnricher_ObjectDisposedExceptionIsHandled_DoesNotEnrich, and no leaked-registration warnings.
